text: Refactoring is the process of improving the internal structure of your code without changing what it does. In other words, the program’s behavior stays exactly the same, but the way the code is written becomes cleaner and more organized. This is important because messy code, often called “technical debt,” becomes harder and harder to read and update over time. By refactoring regularly, you pay off that debt. For example, you might break a long, complicated function into smaller, simpler ones or rename variables to be more descriptive. The main goal is to make your code easier for others—and for your future self—to understand, which saves time and prevents bugs later.
